title: Essential Rent a Car Rules you need to know in UAE
description: Planning to rent a car in Dubai? Learn the essential rent a car rules, required documents, and crucial tips for a smooth car rental experience.

contentHtml:
Before exploring the breathtaking landscapes of the UAE, become fully aware of the essential rent a car rules. It’s more than just driving a car safely. The rules extend from understanding security deposits to handling traffic fines. These updated guidelines for 2025 ensure a hassle-free journey. Choose the perfect vehicle for your adventure and let the roads guide you.

At IZI Rent a Car, we prioritize making your travels smooth and legal. With our expertise in local regulations, we’ve compiled this comprehensive guide to help you avoid pitfalls and maximize your driving experience.

Updated Rules Set by the UAE Government for Car Rentals

Dreaming of cruising through the UAE’s scenic roads? First, familiarize yourself with the rent a car rules and regulations that keep everything in order. From licensing to insurance, these requirements ensure your journey is as seamless as possible.

Valid Driver’s License

A valid and active driver’s license is the primary requirement for renting a car in the UAE. Whereas, in the case of being a tourist, an International Driving Permit (IDP) is required along with their national license. Both documents must comply with local laws and remain valid throughout your rental period. 

  • Residents: Must hold a valid UAE driving license.
  • Tourists: Need a valid home country license + International Driving Permit (IDP).
  • Exceptions: Visitors from GCC, the US, the UK, Europe, Canada, and some Asian countries may be allowed without an IDP (check before booking).

Minimum Age Requirements

The age criteria set by the government are 21 years old to rent a car in the UAE. Many companies require drivers to be 25 or older, especially for premium vehicles. Younger drivers may face additional charges, so confirm with your provider beforehand. 

Mandatory Insurance

Basic insurance is determined to be essential by the government. Therefore, it is essential to always verify the details before renting a car. You can also opt for additional coverage, which adds another layer of protection against Collision Damage Waiver (CDW), Super CDW, and Theft Protection, ensuring peace of mind. The car rental rules about insurance are a must to understand if you want to be free from unexpected financial burdens.

Security Deposit

A refundable security deposit, typically held on your credit card, is standard practice. The amount varies depending on the vehicle and rental company, covering potential fines or damages. Familiarizing yourself with the car rental deposit policies ensures smooth financial transactions.

  • Standard: AED 1,000 – AED 5,000 (refundable).
  • Held on a credit card (some companies accept debit cards or cash).
  • Refund time: 7–21 working days, depending on fines & Salik tolls.

Responsibility for Traffic Fines

The person who rents a car is responsible for any traffic violations that occur during the rental period. Upon non-compliance, rental companies may deduct fines from your deposit or charge your credit card.  Sometimes, they add administrative fees. Staying vigilant about driving tips can help you avoid unnecessary penalties.

Prohibited Activities

Rental agreements declared a few activities to be prohibited. This can include racing, off-roading, or using the car for commercial purposes. In case of breaching these terms and conditions, your insurance might get canceled, and additional penalties would be imposed. Adhering to car rental rules protects you from unforeseen costs.

Vehicle Inspection

Always inspect the vehicle before driving off. Document any pre-existing damages with photos or videos to avoid disputes when returning the car. Verify spare tire, first-aid kit, and fuel level. Thorough checks ensure you’re not held accountable for prior issues.

Key Considerations When Renting a Car

Understand the important aspects of renting a car in the UAE. These important rent a car rules will keep you on the right track, following the safety measures. Avoid surprises and additional costs.

Cross-Border Travel

Thinking about driving beyond UAE borders? Not all rental cars are allowed to cross international boundaries. Special permissions and extra insurance may be required—check with your rental company. Understanding car rental features like international permissions can be crucial for planning.

Salik Tolls and Fines

Dubai’s Salik tolls are automatically charged to your rental vehicle. Vehicle rental Dubai companies handle toll payments, but may include service fees, so clarify this beforehand to avoid surprises. Knowing how these tolls affect your car rental deposit can prevent unexpected charges.

Handling Accidents

Instantly inform the local police authority ( call 999) as well as the car rental company if you are in an accident. Not reporting can lead to significant fines or complications with insurance claims. Quick action ensures compliance with car rental rules and regulations.

Hidden Fees

Familiarize yourself with potential extra charges, including fees for late returns, additional drivers, fuel, or cleaning. Reviewing the rental agreement thoroughly can save you from unexpected deductions. These car rental rules help you budget effectively.

Understanding Return Policies

Be clear on return policies regarding fuel levels, mileage limits, and timing. Adhering to these terms ensures a smooth handover and avoids penalties. Keeping track of car rental features like mileage limits simplifies your trip planning.

Alcohol and Drug Restrictions

There’s a zero-tolerance policy for alcohol and drug consumption. It is strictly prohibited to drive under the influence in the UAE. The driver would have to face severe penalties, including hefty fines, license suspension, and even imprisonment, so always stay sober behind the wheel. Following these driving tips is essential for safety and legality.

Seatbelt and Child Safety

Ensure everyone in the car wears seatbelts (mandatory for all passengers). For families, child seats are required for kids under 4 years. When booking to comply with the UAE’s stringent safety laws. These measures align with car rental rules and promote a secure journey.

Why Renting a Car in the UAE is a Great Choice

Renting a car is a convenient option for traveling, offering unmatched flexibility. Unlike in public transportation, you won’t be restricted to certain areas. Explore the UAE’s iconic landmarks at your own pace with a suitable rental car. Ideal for tourists, businessmen, and residents, renting a car is a budget-friendly option. With updated rent a car rules in UAE, your experience can be smooth and enjoyable.

Driving Tips for a Safe Journey

  1. Obey Speed Limits: The UAE has a strict speed restriction policy, monitored by radars. Avoid fines by adhering to posted limits.
  2. Plan Routes in Advance: Use GPS or maps to navigate efficiently. Many rental cars come equipped with advanced car rental features like built-in navigation.
  3. Stay Alert: Traffic in urban areas can be dense. Defensive driving helps you stay safe.
  4. Avoid Peak Hours: Traffic can be heavy during the morning and evening rush hours. Plan your trips accordingly.

Additional Considerations for First-Time Renters

If you’re new to renting, here are some extra tips:

  • Ask About Fuel Policies: Some rentals require you to return the car with a full tank, while others don’t. Clarify to avoid extra fees.
  • Check Mileage Limits: Some rental agreements have mileage caps. Plan your trips to stay within the limits.
  • Review Terms for Extra Drivers: Adding drivers may incur extra costs. Ensure all drivers meet the car rental rules and regulations.
  • Documents Required for Tourists: Passport, visa copy, IDP (if required), home country license, and credit card.

Conclusion

By understanding these vital rent a car rules in UAE, you’re set to explore the country’s wonders with confidence and ease. From insurance details to toll management, being informed keeps your journey stress-free. So, pick your ideal car, stay compliant, and hit the road for an unforgettable adventure. Happy driving!

FAQs

Who can rent and drive a car in the UAE?

To rent a car, a person should be at least 21 years old or older in some cases. A valid driver’s license or an international Driving Permit is also mandatory. The home country license would also be required if you’re a visitor.

Is an IDP necessary for car rentals?

Visitors typically need an IDP unless they’re from GCC countries. UAE residents with a valid UAE license do not require one.

Can tourists rent a car without an Emirates ID?

Yes, tourists can rent a car using their passport, visa, and International Driving Permit if required.

What should I check before renting a car?

Inspect the vehicle for damage, review the rental agreement, and understand policies on deposits, mileage, and fuel. These steps ensure a smooth experience.

Are there additional fees for younger drivers?

Yes, drivers under 25 may face extra charges depending on the rental company. Confirm this before booking.

Can I rent a car without a credit card in UAE?

Some companies allow debit cards or cash, but credit cards are preferred for security deposits.

How long does it take to get my deposit back?

Typically, 7–21 working days after settling all fines and Salik charges.
